question: How do the Qwen base, chat, code and math models compare with open-source and proprietary models, and how were they built?
contributions: Base Qwen models (1.8B, 7B, 14B) trained on up to 3 trillion tokens
Qwen-Chat models aligned with SFT and RLHF, with tool-use and agent ability

method.summary: A series of decoder-only LLMs (LLaMA-style modified Transformer) pretrained on up to 3T tokens with a ~152K BPE vocabulary built from cl100k_base, then aligned with SFT and PPO-based RLHF, and specialised for code and math by continued pretraining and SFT.
method.task: autoregressive pretraining, SFT, RLHF, code/math specialisation

datasets.name: Qwen pretraining corpus
datasets.source: public web documents, encyclopedia, books, codes, etc.; multilingual, mostly English and Chinese; includes high-quality instruction data
datasets.preprocessing: HTML text extraction, language ID, exact-match dedup after normalisation, MinHash+LSH fuzzy dedup, rule and model-based quality filters, up-sampling of some sources, removal of samples with 13-gram overlap with test sets (for instruction data of reported tasks)

datasets.name: SFT agent data
datasets.source: self-instruct with ReAct format, filtered by rules and humans

models.name: Qwen-1.8B
models.tokenizer: BPE, tiktoken cl100k_base extended, digits split singly

training.objective: next-token prediction (pretraining and SFT, loss masked on system/user inputs); RLHF with PPO; reward model with pooling layer on end token
training.lr: 3.0e-4 peak for all three base sizes (Table 1); SFT peak 2e-6; reward model constant 3e-6; PPO policy 1e-6, value 5e-6; Code-Qwen 6.0e-5 (14B), 3.0e-5 (7B); Code SFT 2.0e-6 (14B), 1.0e-5 (7B); Math SFT 2e-5
training.lr_schedule: pretraining cosine decaying to 10% of peak; Code-Qwen pretraining no decay; Code SFT cosine warmup then constant
training.warmup: SFT: first 1430 steps; Code-Qwen 3% warm-up iterations; Code SFT 3% warm-up steps
training.seq_len: pretraining 2048; SFT 2048; reward 2048; Code-Qwen up to 8192; Math SFT 1024
training.precision: BFloat16 mixed precision; FP32 for RoPE inverse frequency matrix
training.regularisation: gradient clipping 1.0 (SFT); PPO KL coefficient 0.04, value loss clip 0.15, pretrained-gradient term against alignment tax

other.architecture changes: untied embeddings, RoPE, bias removed except QKV, pre-norm RMSNorm, SwiGLU with FFN dim 8/3 of hidden, Flash Attention
other.reward model: initialised from same-size pretrained Qwen; ~6600 tags classification system for prompts
other.PPO: value model only updated for first 50 steps; 2 responses sampled per query; reward normalised by running mean; top-p 0.9

inference.decoding: greedy for math (Table 12); PPO policy top-p 0.9
inference.prompting: MMLU 5-shot, C-Eval 5-shot, GSM8K 8-shot, MATH 4-shot, HumanEval 0-shot, MBPP 0-shot, BBH 3-shot for base; chat zero-shot and few-shot; ReAct prompting for tools

parameters.context extension: training-free dynamic NTK-aware interpolation, LogN-Scaling, layer-wise window attention (shorter windows in lower layers)

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: benchmark accuracy (MMLU, C-Eval, GSM8K, MATH, BBH)

metrics.name: human win rate vs GPT-3.5
metrics.definition: 3 annotators rank responses on 300 Chinese instructions

eval.protocol: Baseline scores copied from official reports and OpenCompass (higher of reported and leaderboard); single run, no seeds or significance tests stated.
